newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Crewmen plucked from Indian Ocean as ship sinks.
newsitem.headline: Crewmen plucked from Indian Ocean as ship sinks.

text.p: A Romanian cargo ship sank off the Indian Ocean coast of South Africa on Friday and rescue helicopters plucked 20 of its 21 crew members from heavy seas, rescue officials said.

The Liberian-registered Calarasi, owned by the Navrom company of Constanza, went down in heavy seas about 10 miles off Port St Johns on the Wild Coast of Transkei. First reports had said there were 22 crew members aboard.
Two South African Air Force helicopters carried out the rescue and a doctor on the rescue team reported no injuries.
"The helicopters have rescued 20 people now," Captain Joy Rautenbach told Reuters. "A helicopter will remain in the area as long as the weather permits to search for those still missing."
"The pilots reported to us when they picked up the first 12 survivors that the ship had sunk," she said. Those rescued were all Romanians.
There was no immediate information on the port of origin or destination of the Calarasi.

The 4,800 dwt freighter lost power due to engine problems and began drifting. A distress signal was received by South Africa's National Sea Rescue Institute and a tug from the port of East London was sent to the area.
